finding.claim: Broken access control on /admin/drop: the role check result is discarded, so any authenticated user can reach a destructive DROP TABLE.
finding.source: Any request whose context carries a *User (set by middleware not in this tree; api.go:22-25)

trace.note: /admin/drop registered with no route-level role check
u := userFrom(r); any user from context is accepted
Authorize(u, "dba") return value ignored; a 'forbidden' error does not stop execution
DROP TABLE executes regardless of role

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error for non-dba users, but the caller ignores it (contrast vacuum at api.go:33-36, which checks it). No other guard on this path in the visible code. Route has no method or role wrapper. Auth middleware is not in the tree, so whether an unauthenticated request can get a *User in context is unknown.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only role check, and its error return is discarded at api.go:26 as a bare statement. The vacuum handler (api.go:33-36) does check it, so the omission in dropTable is a real gap. No route-level wrapper exists at api.go:44. The only remaining precondition is that a *User is present in context, which is set by middleware not in this tree. userFrom (api.go:22) panics without one, so anonymous requests cannot reach the sink.
verdict.reason: The role check at api.go:26 is a bare call whose error is discarded, so runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 runs for any authenticated user who lacks the dba role, and the route at api.go:44 has no other guard. Trace lines 44, 25, 26, 27 and 28 all match the code.

finding.claim: SQL injection in the DROP TABLE statement: the table name is concatenated from a request parameter with no validation, quoting, or allowlist.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 (query string or form body, fully attacker-controlled)

trace.note: t taken from FormValue and concatenated into the SQL string
runSQL is a stub here; if it executes via a driver that accepts multiple statements, stacked queries are possible

finding.guards_checked: None. No identifier validation, regex, allowlist, or quoting. The DBA role check is bypassed by F1 but would not stop injection in any case. Impact depends on runSQL's real implementation, which is not in this tree.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize at api.go:26 is a bare statement whose error return is discarded, so it blocks nothing. No identifier validation, allowlist, quoting, or parameterization is applied to r.FormValue("t") before it is concatenated at api.go:27. runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so the injection's real impact depends on the production runSQL, which is not in this tree.
verdict.reason: The source at api.go:27 is concatenated unescaped into a SQL string passed to runSQL (api.go:27, api.go:41 takes a raw string), and the route at api.go:44 is reachable by any authenticated user because the Authorize result at api.go:26 is discarded, so no effective control stops the injection. Exploitability in production still depends on runSQL's real implementation, which this tree does not contain.
